name: Cessna 177 Cardinal
summary: Cessna's strutless successor-that-wasn't to the 172: a four-seat cantilever high-wing with a stabilator, steeply raked windshield and sleek lines. The 177RG adds retractable gear.

wings: Cantilever high wing with no lift struts
Tapered wing mounted well aft of the windshield
engines: Single flat-four in a smoothly tapered, low cowling
fuselage: Steeply raked windshield and wide, bubble-like cabin glazing
Fixed tricycle gear (177/177B) or retractable tricycle gear (177RG)
Pilot sits ahead of the wing leading edge
tail: Swept fin with a dorsal fillet
All-flying stabilator in place of separate stabilizer and elevator

tellTales: High wing with no struts at all
Steeply raked windshield and a sleek, sloping nose
Swept fin with a one-piece moving horizontal tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The 177 has a strutless cantilever wing, a stabilator and a raked windshield; the 172 has a lift strut on each wing and a conventional tail.
The 182 has lift struts and a deeper, blunter cowl; the 177 has a clean wing with no struts and a smoother nose.
The 177RG is a strutless four-seater with a small cowl and a one-piece stabilator; the 210 is a larger six-seater with a bigger cowl and a conventional tail.
The 177 is a high-wing aluminium aircraft; the SR20/22 is a low-wing composite with a parachute hatch behind the cabin.
